headline: California has banned employers from using AI systems as the only basis for disciplining or firing workers, with the rules starting on 1 July 2027.
score_reason: Lowered from 5: the law was signed on 30 Sep, so this is older news re-reported.
importance_line: It affects California workers and employers who use scoring software in HR, but the law does not define "primarily relies", so how strictly it will be applied is open.
summary: PPC Land reports that Governor Gavin Newsom signed SB 947 on 30 Sep 2026, which from 1 July 2027 bars California employers from relying solely on automated decision systems to discipline or fire staff, and requires a human to check any AI-driven decision against other evidence and tell the worker in writing that software was involved. The state Labor Commissioner can investigate and fine employers $500 per violation.
notes: Older news re-dated by the outlet; law signed 30 Sep 2026.
